newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to issue zero coupons to help mkt-paper.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to issue zero coupons to help mkt-paper.

text.p: The Thai government is set to issue zero coupon bonds in an effort to revitalise the sagging stock market which has suffered following a finance sector shake-up this week, a local newspaper reported on Friday.

The Bangkok Post reported finance ministry officials as saying the decision to issue the bonds was made late on Thursday. The newspaper said all the zero coupon bonds would be sold to foreign investors.

The Bangkok Post said the decision to issue the bonds was reached during a dinner meeting between Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan and former premier and Chart Pattana party leader Chatichai Choonhavan.
Chatichai also holds the position of senior advisor for economic affairs to the government. The Chart Pattana party is the second-largest member of the coalition government.
The newspaper gave no further details of the issue. Ministry officials were not immediately available for comment.

Thai markets have suffered this week after the government on Monday announced a major shake-up of the financial sector by ordering 10 finance firms facing liquidity problems to boost their capital by a total of 8.25 billion baht ($317 million).
Authorities also told banks and finance companies to raise provisions for bad loans, made mainly to the depressed property sector, to 115 and 120 percent, respectively, from 100 percent previously.
Financial institutions are also required to set aside a total of 50 billion baht in additional provisions.
The revamp sent shockwaves through the system, prompting investors to withdraw billions of baht from the 10 firms and other financial institutions, a central bank official said.
